papers.title_en: MM-Net: A Multimodal Multi-Task Network for Sleep Staging and Sleep Apnea Assessment After Ischemic Stroke
papers.authors: Md Wahiduzzaman Suva, Esm E Moula Chowdhury Abha, Md Imtiaj Alam Sajin, Md Iftekharul Mobin, Jia Uddin
papers.evidence: 卒中后多模态EEG睡眠分期解码
papers.tldr: 针对缺血性脑卒中后联合睡眠分期与呼吸事件分析不足及预训练EEG编码器表示不一致问题，提出多模态多任务框架MM-Net。通过交叉拟合与岭回归嵌入对齐，融合EEG-EOG表征、神经描述符与心肺特征，在iSLEEPS上取得76.3%分期准确率和0.825呼吸AUC，优于基线，并在多个数据集验证有效性。
papers.abstract_en: Automated polysomnography after ischemic stroke is challenging because of altered sleep-related neural activity and concurrent respiratory disturbances. Existing stroke-specific approaches mainly address sleep-stage classification, leaving joint analysis of sleep architecture and respiratory events underexplored. Moreover, adapting pretrained EEG encoders introduces a representation inconsistency when downstream models are trained on embeddings from previously seen patients but evaluated on unseen individuals. We propose MM-Net, a multimodal multi-task framework that resolves this inconsistency through cross-fitting and ridge-based embedding alignment. Sleep-adapted EEG-EOG representations and engineered neural descriptors are fused with learned cardiorespiratory features through cross-attention and shared temporal modeling for simultaneous sleep staging and respiratory-event detection. On iSLEEPS (99 patients with subacute ischemic stroke), ten-fold patient-independent evaluation achieved 76.3% staging accuracy (Cohen's $κ$ = 0.656) and 0.825 respiratory-event AUC, outperforming the evaluated baselines under matched protocols. The sleep-adapted encoder improved the downstream model when its embeddings were aligned, raising staging accuracy by 1.4 percentage points over the frozen encoder ($p$ = 0.020) versus 0.2 points without alignment. MM-Net also achieved 86.4% staging accuracy on Sleep-EDF, above every single-EEG architecture reimplemented on the same recordings, and 80.3% staging accuracy with 0.889 respiratory AUC on ISRUC-I, exceeding its retrained staging baselines. Without retraining, the iSLEEPS-trained model retained respiratory AUCs of 0.833 on ISRUC-I and 0.841 on UCD. These findings support representation-consistent neural adaptation and joint physiological modeling across stroke, healthy-sleep, and sleep-disorder cohorts.

papers.title_en: Neuronal Identity as an Organizational Basis for Analyzing Neural Population Dynamics
papers.authors: Seungjae Han, Joshua Yedam You, Soi Kim, Minho Eom, Jinho Park, Seunghee Park, Byeongwook Lee, Young-Gyu Yoon
papers.evidence: 利用生物学特征跨会话对齐神经群体动态
papers.tldr: 个体神经元的多模态生物特征在个体间共享但未被充分利用。本研究提出新框架，基于这些生物特征将神经元路由到潜在组，通过组级表示分析群体动力学，从而支持跨个体迁移而无需重新训练或神经元级对应。在斑马鱼全脑钙成像和小鼠视觉皮层电生理上验证，该框架在神经解码和流形分析上均优于基线，表明用生物特征显式组织神经群体是有效的。
papers.abstract_en: Individual neurons exhibit diverse molecular, morphological, and electrophysiological properties that shape their distinct roles in neural circuits. While these multimodal features are largely shared across individuals, they remain an underutilized source of information in analyzing neural population dynamics. We posit that these shared biological profiles provide a common reference for relating neural dynamics across subjects and recording sessions. Our framework leverages this structure by routing neurons into latent groups based on their biological profiles and analyzing population dynamics through group-level representations. Because these assignments are anchored in biological properties that are consistent across subjects, the learned organization supports transfer to unseen animals without retraining or neuron-wise correspondence. We evaluate our framework on whole-brain calcium imaging in larval zebrafish and large-scale electrophysiology in the mouse visual cortex. Across both species and recording modalities, the framework delivers state-of-the-art performance in both neural decoding and manifold analysis: it achieves superior decoding of behavior and stimulus labels while better preserving the temporal consistency and local geometric structure of latent trajectories on unseen data. Our experiments demonstrate that not only does providing biological features improve baseline performance, but our proposed framework achieves even stronger results by using these properties to explicitly structure the population rather than treating them as auxiliary inputs. Together, these results suggest that organizing neural populations by their multimodal biological features offers a promising framework for generalizing population dynamics across subjects and recording sessions.

papers.title_en: Comparing Temporal Deep Learning Architectures for Discrete Cross-User Myoelectric Control
papers.authors: Ethan Eddy, Evan Campbell, Scott Bateman, Erik Scheme
papers.evidence: 肌电控制的时间深度学习
papers.tldr: 本研究针对离散跨用户肌电控制，基于612人EMG-EPN数据集，基准测试五种时序深度学习架构，发现CNN-GRU最优，在184名新用户上准确率93%，并进一步在五年后不同国家采集的未分段真实数据集上验证，准确率达96%，证明零样本跨用户离散肌电控制潜力。
papers.abstract_en: The recognition of dynamic gestures via discrete myoelectric control is becoming an attractive input modality for event-based human-machine interaction. While recent work suggests that discrete cross-user models are possible (i.e., no calibration data is required from the end user), few have evaluated techniques to optimize these systems and their generalizability to new randomly prompted data simulating real-world discrete control is relatively unknown. Using the 612-user EMG-EPN dataset, this work benchmarks five temporal deep-learning approaches, evaluates the tradeoff between performance and model complexity, and compares hand-crafted and machine-learned feature extraction techniques. The CNN-GRU achieved the best accuracy of 93% when tested on 184 previously unseen users. These models were then evaluated on a different, more realistic, unsegmented dataset, wherein users were randomly prompted to elicit discrete gestures during a continuous data collection. This dataset was recorded five years apart and in a separate country from the data used to train the original model. Results show that the cross-user results scale to this new dataset (accuracies of 96%) even though no feedback was given to users during the elicitation of gestures. These findings highlight the exciting potential of discrete zero-shot cross-user myoelectric control and offer valuable insights for the continued advancement of this promising technology.

papers.title_en: Cross-User Adaptation for sEMG Gesture Recognition via Continual Learning
papers.authors: Aran Ramakrishnan, Shubhi Mishra, Tyler Ham, Assel Kembay, Jason Eshraghian
papers.evidence: 使用持续学习进行跨用户sEMG手势识别自适应
papers.tldr: 针对sEMG手势识别跨用户适应，本研究在NinaPro DB1上评估持续学习策略。经验回放优于EWC和朴素微调，类增量漂移下准确率83.3%，遗忘仅1.8-5.8%。模型需以打乱独立窗口训练，时序流导致崩溃；手工时域特征提升精度约40%，仅回放保持增益。
papers.abstract_en: Prosthetic and assistive interfaces increasingly depend on decoding hand gestures from surface electromyography (sEMG). Because the signal is shaped by person-specific factors, the recurrent neural networks (RNNs) commonly used to model these temporal streams must adapt to new wearers and new gesture classes after deployment. Continual learning (CL) enables this adaptation without retraining from scratch, yet applying it to recurrent sEMG models is not straightforward. Standard recurrent training practices can destabilize learning, and which CL strategy holds up under realistic cross-user drift is unestablished. We evaluate three representative CL strategies under domain- and class-incremental drift on NinaPro DB1, and find experience replay to outperform elastic weight consolidation (EWC) and naive fine-tuning. It reaches 83.3% final accuracy for class-incremental drift while limiting forgetting to 1.8-5.8% accuracy drop, as against 16.2-28.5% for EWC and naive training. We further show these models must be trained on shuffled, independently-windowed segments. Streaming windows in temporal order collapses the network into predicting a single dominant gesture, while a shuffled, stateless regime trains stably. Finally, hand-crafted time-domain features raise per-task accuracy by up to about 40% over raw signals, but only replay preserves that gain under class-incremental drift.

papers.title_en: Revisiting entropy and entropy-related magnitudes of a symbolic sequence and their estimation
papers.authors: Efren Aragon-Perez, Ania Mesa-Rodriguez, Karel Garcia-Medina, Daniel Estevez-Moya, Amanda Mollineda-Rodriguez, Ernesto Estevez-Rams
papers.evidence: 提供符号序列的熵估计方法，可用于神经脉冲序列分析
papers.tldr: 本文重新审视符号序列的熵及相关量（熵密度、有效测量复杂度、信息距离），结合信息论与遍历论建立数学基础，连接香农熵与柯尔莫哥洛夫复杂度。基于Ziv定理证明归一化不同词数与熵密度渐近等价，提出有限序列估计方法及开源并行Lempel-Ziv分解库，并通过脑功能连接、非线性振荡器和房颤分类三个案例展示其效用。
papers.abstract_en: This article revisits entropy and related magnitudes (entropy density, effective measure complexity, and informational distance) for the analysis of sequential data. We present their mathematical foundations within information theory and ergodic theory, establishing connections between probabilistic Shannon entropy and algorithmic Kolmogorov complexity. A central result, Zivs theorem, demonstrates the asymptotic equivalence between the normalised number of distinct words and entropy density, providing the theoretical basis for estimation via Lempel-Ziv factorisation. We examine the convergence properties of these magnitudes and introduce estimation procedures for finite sequences, including a method for the effective measure complexity and the transfer entropy rate. An open-source software library implementing parallel algorithms for efficient Lempel-Ziv factorisation is presented. The practical utility of the framework is illustrated through three case studies: functional brain connectivity analysis from fMRI data, characterisation of spatiotemporal dynamics in coupled nonlinear oscillators, and electrocardiogram-based classification of atrial fibrillation, demonstrating how entropic measures capture meaningful structural and dynamical properties across diverse domains.

papers.title_en: LUCID: Local Understanding of Covariate Importance with Conditional Density Estimation
papers.authors: Yixiao Wang, Srikar Katta, Jon Donnelly, Emanuele Borgonovo, Cynthia Rudin
papers.evidence: 可应用于解释神经编码模型的模型无关局部变量重要性方法
papers.tldr: 针对局部变量重要性评估中特征依赖被忽视的问题，本文提出模型无关的LUCID方法，利用条件密度估计从全条件分布采样进行特征扰动，生成合理反事实。作者建立了与现有VI测度的理论联系，并提供具有收敛保证和不确定性量化的估计器，模拟与真实数据验证了其稳定性和实用性。
papers.abstract_en: Computing local-level variable importance (VI) is critical for understanding machine learning models. Local permutation-based VI metrics offer a simple yet powerful approach, measuring how much a model's output changes when perturbing its inputs. However, existing perturbation strategies often ignore feature dependence or account for it only through restricted approximations. Perturbing a feature without fully respecting this dependence can generate unrealistic counterfactuals, thereby evaluating the model in regions unsupported by the observed data distribution. We address this gap by introducing a new model-agnostic local VI metric and estimator, Local Understanding of Covariate Importance with conditional Density estimation (LUCID). LUCID perturbs features of interest using plausible values drawn from the full conditional distribution given the remaining observed features. We establish theoretical connections between LUCID and existing VI measures, and provide an estimator with convergence guarantees and uncertainty quantification. Finally, we demonstrate LUCID's stable performance and practical utility across simulated and real-world examples.

papers.title_en: Physiology-Informed Audio Quality and Listening Effort Estimation
papers.evidence: 使用EEG和fNIRS估计音频质量和听音努力
papers.tldr: 本研究探索用消费级生理设备（可穿戴 EEG、fNIRS、眼动仪）替代实验室级设备来估计音频质量和聆听努力。通过记录三十名听众聆听时的生理信号，发现商用可穿戴和光学传感能显著解码音频质量，并能按个体校准跟踪聆听努力，为个性化音频平台提供可能。
papers.abstract_en: Audio systems aim to maximise the listener's perceived quality, traditionally evaluated through mean opinion scoring (MOS), a subjective process that is slow, costly, and collected only after playback. Machine learning now predicts MOS directly from the audio, but in generalising across participants it tends to discard the subject variance that defines individual perception. Neurophysiological measures may offer a complementary signal taken directly from the listener, objective, implicit, and continuous, though prior work has relied on laboratory-grade EEG and fNIRS. We ask how practical consumer-grade devices compare, and whether they might recover population-level audio-quality trends and, when calibrated per listener, track that listener's effort. Recording 32-channel laboratory EEG alongside wearable EEG, fNIRS, and eye tracking from thirty listeners, our results suggest commercial wearable and optical sensing can decode audio quality at statistically significant levels and recover listening effort per listener. These findings may point towards platforms tuned not only to perceived quality but to the effort a clip demands, read from the listener's own response as they listen.
